issues.description: Real-time pacing claimed in changelog but no pacing logic exists in the diff
issues.detail: The changelog promises 'real-time pacing' for media endpoints like Vonage Audio Connector, but _write_frame just drains the buffer in a tight while-loop and fires every full chunk back-to-back. That is packetization, not pacing. Either remove the 'real-time pacing' claim or add the sleep/scheduler that actually paces sends. Don't ship docs that lie about what the code does.

issues.description: fixed_audio_packet_size silently mutates non-audio binary payloads
issues.detail: The buffering branch triggers on any bytes/bytearray payload, not just audio. If a serializer ever emits a binary control message (or a future frame type does), it gets chopped into PCM-sized chunks and corrupted. Gate this on the frame being an AudioRawFrame, or have the serializer mark audio explicitly. Right now the abstraction has no idea what it is buffering.

issues.description: Tail audio is never flushed; last sub-packet is dropped on stream end
issues.detail: Remainder bytes sit in _audio_send_buffer forever unless another audio frame arrives that pushes the buffer back over threshold. On end-of-stream or long silences the final partial packet is silently discarded. Either pad-and-flush on EndFrame/CancelFrame or document that trailing audio shorter than one packet is dropped. Currently neither is done.

issues.description: DTMF parsing invents a second wire format with no evidence Vonage emits it
issues.detail: deserialize() reads digit from either message['digit'] or message['dtmf']['digit']. This is exactly the bad-taste pattern: a special case added on speculation. Pick the shape Vonage actually sends, cite it, and delete the other branch. If both genuinely occur, link the doc in a comment. Otherwise this is a guess that every future reader has to re-verify.

issues.description: Rename of audio_packet_bytes to fixed_audio_packet_size is a breaking change with no deprecation
issues.detail: The changed.md entry renames a public param. If audio_packet_bytes ever shipped, downstream users break on upgrade with no shim or warning. If it never shipped, the changelog line is noise and should be dropped. Either alias the old name with a DeprecationWarning or stop advertising a rename that nobody needs to know about.

issues.description: Zero tests for either the serializer or the packetization buffer
issues.detail: New protocol serializer, new stateful buffer in the transport, interruption-clears-buffer behavior, remainder handling - none of it has a test. The packet-boundary math (640 bytes = 20ms @ 16kHz PCM16) is exactly the kind of off-by-one that surfaces in production six months later. Add a unit test that feeds odd-sized payloads and asserts chunk boundaries plus interruption-clear behavior.

review.summary: Patch does two things at once - new Vonage serializer plus a generic packetization buffer in FastAPIWebsocketTransport - and the buffer is the part that needs work. It mutates any binary payload regardless of whether it's audio, never flushes the tail, and the 'real-time pacing' the changelog promises isn't actually in the code. The serializer is mostly fine but invents a dual DTMF format on speculation and ships with no tests. NEEDS-WORK: gate the buffer on audio frames, flush on end-of-stream, drop the pacing claim or implement it, and add tests for the chunk-boundary math.
